The second edition of the India Art, Architecture and Design Biennale (IAADB) will be held from 4th December 2026 to 21st March 2027 in New Delhi.The theme of this 108-day Biennale is ‘Tat Tvam Asi – Reconnecting in an Age of Distraction’. Talking exclusively to Akashvani News, Secretary of the Ministry of Culture, Vivek Aggarwal said that, the Biennale will feature art installations at iconic heritage sites of the National Capital, including Purana Qila, Red Fort, Safdarjung Tomb, Qutub Minar, Qila Rai Pithora and Lodhi Garden. He said that the theme of this year’s Biennale directly takes inspiration from India’s ancient traditions and spiritual thought, which emphasize self-introspection and the unity of the individual with the larger universal consciousness.Mr Aggarwal said that the Ministry aims to take IAADB to a global level by encouraging participation from international pavilions and artists, Indian states and the private sector.Speaking about the cultural diplomacy of India, He said that cultural exchange is an important component of cultural diplomacy and the country’s soft power. Mr Aggarwal added that participation of foreign countries will provide an opportunity for Indian and international audiences to experience diverse art forms and will help position the Biennale on the global cultural calendar.Underlining the importance of Art and Design students in this Biennale, He said that the Ministry plans to involve students, particularly those pursuing art and design, in various activities associated with the Biennale, providing them opportunities to engage with artists and the wider creative ecosystem.The second edition of the India Art, Architecture & Design Biennale 2026 is the largest platform which offers artists, curators, galleries, corporates, architects, designers, cultural institutions and other stakeholders a chance to connect with culture and the creative world. This edition is conceived not as a single exhibition in a single location but as a city-wide cultural platform. Visitors will have an opportunity to experience the historical monuments along with contemporary art installations.

. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has removed Paytm Payments Bank Ltd (PPBL) from the list of scheduled banks following the cancellation of its banking licence. The RBI said PPBL has been excluded from the Second Schedule to the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. The notification was published on July 31 and later notified in the Gazette of India.The central bank had cancelled PPBL’s banking licence in April for non-compliance with regulatory norms, stating that the bank’s affairs were being conducted in a manner detrimental to the interests of depositors.The Delhi High Court subsequently ordered the winding up of Paytm Payments Bank.PPBL has faced several regulatory restrictions in recent years. In March 2022, the RBI barred the bank from onboarding new customers following supervisory concerns. Further restrictions were imposed in January and February 2024, including a ban on accepting fresh deposits, credits and top-ups in customer accounts, prepaid instruments and wallets.

. In Ladakh, RNU Akashvani Kargil has launched a special podcast series under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, with the first programme focusing on “Natural Farming – Towards Sustainable and Climate-Resilient Agriculture.”The programme featured Dr. Nazir Hussain, Scientist, Krishi Vigyan Kendra Kargil, in conversation with Anayat Ali of RNU Akashvani Kargil.During the podcast, Dr. Nazir Hussain explained the principles of natural farming and highlighted its role in improving soil health, reducing dependence on external chemical inputs and promoting sustainable and climate-resilient agriculture.He discussed various aspects of the National Mission on Natural Farming, including chemical-free cultivation, livestock integration, diversified cropping, use of locally available bio-inputs and integration of traditional agricultural knowledge with scientific practices.Dr. Hussain said natural farming has considerable potential in Ladakh and Kargil, where agriculture is characterised by a short growing season, cold climatic conditions and limited water availability. He stressed the need for locally adapted practices, scientific research, farmer training and awareness for its successful adoption in the region.Comparing natural farming with organic farming, Dr. Hussain said natural farming can be more effective and efficient in boosting production while reducing farmers’ dependence on externally purchased inputs.The discussion also covered crop productivity, input costs, farmers’ income, water management, climate resilience and the need to make the transition towards natural farming economically viable for farmers.The special podcast series, produced by RNU Akashvani Kargil under the Seva Sankalp Abhiyan, will be broadcast daily at 4:30 PM from Akashvani Kargil. The programmes will also be available on the AIRNews Kargil YouTube channel.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has issued a red colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall with isolated extremely heavy rainfall over Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand tomorrow. According to IMD, heavy to very heavy rainfall is likely over Chhattisgarh and Madhya Pradesh tomorrow. The districts that are likely to receive heavy rainfall include Rampur, Pilibhit, Bareilly, Shahjahanpur and Bahraich. Meanwhile, districts of Madhya Pradesh which are expected to receive rainfall include Satna, Chhatarpur, Tikamgarh and Niwari.IMD said that the line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon continues to pass through Gurdaspur, Chandigarh, Muzaffarnagar, Aligarh, Dholpur, Udaipur, Deesa and Naliya.The Met Department has also predicted heavy rainfall over Delhi, Haryana, Chandigarh, Bihar, Himachal Pradesh, Jharkhand, Odisha, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal and Sikkim for the day. Thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty windsare expectedto prevail over Punjab, Madhya Pradesh, Vidarbha, Andhra Pradesh, Kerala, Mahe, Telangana, Andaman and Nicobar Islands and parts of Northeast during the next two days.Meanwhile, parts of Delhi are expected to witness light to moderate rainfall tomorrow.

. The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry has been awarded to French chemist Henri B. Kagan and Japanese chemist Kenso Soai for their pioneering discoveries of non-linear effects and autocatalysis in asymmetric organic synthesis. The Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences today said Kagan and Soai solved a century-old mystery of how molecular asymmetry, or homochirality, can emerge spontaneously in nature.Many molecules, including amino acids, exist in two mirror-image forms. While these variants are chemically similar, living organisms overwhelmingly use only one form. For decades, scientists struggled to understand how such selectivity emerged naturally.According to the Nobel Committee, chemists traditionally obtained equal amounts of both mirror-image molecules during laboratory synthesis. The discoveries by Kagan and Soai demonstrated how chemical reactions can be steered toward producing predominantly or even exclusively one mirror image.This is a breakthrough with major implications for modern chemistry, particularly pharmaceutical development where the correct molecular form is often crucial for therapeutic effectiveness. Kagan made a major breakthrough in 1986 by developing a method to influence chemical reactions to produce a higher excess of one molecular mirror image, while Soai built on this work with a groundbreaking reaction in 1995 and in 2003 demonstrated a reaction producing only one of the two possible mirror-image forms.The two laureates will share a prize of 12 million Swedish kronor.

The UAE has started implementing new limits on sodium, processed sugar and fat content in selected packaged food products, as part of a national effort to improve nutrition and reduce obesity and other noncommunicable diseases linked to unhealthy diets.The Ministry of Health and Prevention (MoHAP) said the rules apply to locally manufactured and imported packaged foods, as well as food establishments handling these products across the UAE, including free zones. The limits will be introduced in phases, with the final limits to be met by December 31, 2030.The first group includes leavened and flat bread, sweetened milk drinks, flavoured yoghurt and laban, and salty snacks such as crackers, nuts, pretzels and chips. The second group covers processed cheese. The limits vary by product and will become stricter in the final phase.Food establishments must meet the first-phase limits within nine months for the first group and within two years and three months for processed cheese. Products manufactured or imported before the rules took effect can remain on sale for up to one year or until their expiry date, whichever comes first. The rules allow establishments to apply for limited exceptions to the first-phase limits in certain cases, but all targeted products must meet the final limits by the end of 2030.Violations can result in a warning, fines ranging from 5 thousand Emirates Dirham to 5 lakh Dirham, closure of the establishment for up to six months, or cancellation of its licence or approval, depending on the seriousness and recurrence of the violation.

. In Asian markets today, South Korea’s Kospi index fell two per cent, Singapore’s Strait Times index declined over 1.6 per cent, Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped over 0.9 per cent, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng dipped more than 0.6 per cent, and Taiwan’s Taiex ended marginally down. Meanwhile, the market in China remained closed for a holiday.In European markets, Germany’s DAX was trading over 1.4 per cent down, while London’s FTSE 100 fell more than 0.7 per cent, when reports last came in.

. In Table Tennis, Indian paddlers Manush Shah and Diya Chitale created history by becoming the first Indian mixed doubles pair to reach the semifinals of a WTT Grand Smash after beating Romania’s Eduard Ionescu and Bernadette Szocs 3-0 at the China Smash in Beijing yesterday.The fifth-seeded Indian duo won the quarterfinal 11-9, 13-11, 11-3 to secure a place in the last four.However, Manav Thakkar exited the men’s singles in the round of 32 after losing 0-3 to seventh seed Alexis Lebrun of France.In women’s doubles, Diya Chitale and Yashaswini Ghorpade suffered a narrow 2-3 defeat to China’s Gao Yuxin and Xiang Junlin in the round of 16.

. Bhutan Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay has lauded Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s 25 years in public service, describing India’s development journey under his leadership as increasingly significant not only for India but also for its neighbours and the wider Global South. In an article in Hindi Daily, Mr Tobgay said the vision of a Viksit Bharat has implications well beyond India’s borders, particularly for countries such as Bhutan. Mr Tobgay highlighted Prime Minister Modi’s approach of placing India’s neighbours at the centre of the country’s international engagement.  He also praised Modi’s efforts to champion the interests of the Global South, including the convening of the Voice of Global South Summits and India’s successful initiative to bring the African Union into the G20 as a permanent member.According to Mr Tobgay, the philosophy of “B4B”  ‘Bharat for Bhutan’ can now be seen across the Himalayan kingdom. He pointed to India’s support in several sectors, including schools and hospitals, roads and bridges, hydropower, technology, agriculture and enterprise. However, Mr Tobgay said the partnership has become particularly significant as  major development initiatives have been envisioned for the development  of Bhutan. Bhutan Prime Minister said, Mr Modi has pledged India’s full support for the project, and that commitment is already taking shape through cooperation on rail links, border infrastructure, as well as improved air and digital connectivity.Mr Tobgay also recalled the role played by India in Bhutan’s successive Five-Year Plans. He said India’s assistance during Bhutan’s 11th Five-Year Plan helped his first government implement an ambitious development programme. He added that Modi continued the partnership during Bhutan’s 12th Plan. He noted that after his returned to office in 2024, India increased its support for Bhutan’s 13th Five-Year Plan to 10,000 crore rupees. Mr Tobgay also argued that India’s economic growth will have a direct impact on its ability to contribute to the development of neighbouring countries. He recalled that in June 2014, only weeks after becoming Prime Minister of India, Narendra Modi selected Bhutan as the destination for his first foreign visit.

. Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan, Home Minister Amit Shah and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh paid tributes to Lok Nayak Jayaprakash Narayan on his death anniversary.Vice-President Radhakrishnan paid homage to the Bharat Ratna Jayaprakash Narayan at Up-Rashtrapati Bhavan. He recalled his contributions to the freedom struggle, the Quit India Movement, the Bhoodan and Sarvodaya movements, and his call for ‘Sampoorna Kranti’. He said Jayaprakash Narayan’s commitment to social justice, people’s empowerment and democratic values continues to inspire generations.Home Minister Amit Shah said Jayaprakash Narayan fearlessly raised his voice against the Emergency and stood for the protection of democracy. He said his call for ‘Total Revolution’ and his life philosophy remain a source of inspiration.Defence Minister Rajnath Singh said Jayaprakash Narayan’s life was dedicated to democracy, public participation and social change. He highlighted his role in the freedom struggle, the Bhoodan Movement and his efforts to protect democratic rights and civil liberties during the Emergency.

. In Japan Open Tennis, world No. 3 Carlos Alcaraz will face 19th-ranked Jiri Lehecka in the Men’s Singles final in Tokyo today. Alcaraz overcame his Spanish compatriot Jaume Munar in the semifinal to prevail 5-7, 6-3, 6-1. On the other hand, Lehecka of Czech Republic defeated Monégasque Valentin Vacherot 6-4, 6-2 in the second semifinal. In Mens doubles clash, American Austin Krajicek and his Croatian partner Nikola Mektić will face French dou Théo Arribagé and Albano Olivetti in the final today.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Chennai on October 11 to dedicate a metro rail project to the public and participate in other programmes.The Prime Minister is scheduled to inaugurate the 14.6-km Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch in Chennai and Amrit Bharat Stations at Palani, Paramakudi, Namakkal, Ambasamudram and Vellore Cantonment through video conference.He will also inaugurate rail projects worth Rs. 700 crore in Coimbatore. The Prime Minister will hold a road show in Chennai soon after inaugurating the metro rail project from Poonamallee.He will also inaugurate a music research centre established by music maestro and Rajya Sabha MP Ilaiyaraaja.

. The nation is celebrating the 94th anniversary of the Indian Air Force (IAF) today. Established on October 8, 1932, the IAF has played a vital role in safeguarding the nation’s security and supporting humanitarian and disaster relief efforts.On the occasion, President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Home Minister Amit Shah and Defence Minister Rajnath Singh extended greetings to all air warriors, veterans and their families.President Murmu praised the IAF’s professionalism, discipline and preparedness, highlighting the courage and precision demonstrated during Operation Sindoor.Vice President Radhakrishnan lauded the IAF’s valour and dedication, while Prime Minister Modi said the force has demonstrated its strength and capability in safeguarding the nation’s skies. He highlighted the induction of advanced technologies, data and drones to counter emerging threats.Home Minister Amit Shah praised the IAF’s valour, precision and striking capabilities. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh described the force as a symbol of courage, discipline and professionalism, and praised its unwavering commitment to national security.

. A massive Russian strike killed 25 people and injured 100 others in Ukraine yesterday. Russia launched 70 missiles alongside dozens of attack drones targeting Kyiv and a dozen other Ukrainian regions. The heaviest toll occurred in Pryluky in the northern Chernihiv region, where a missile obliterated a five-story apartment building, killing 19 people. Additional civilian deaths and damage were reported in Kyiv, Oleksandria, and Kremenchuk.According to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, Ukrainian forces intercepted 44 missiles and suppressed 117 drones, though they were unable to fend off the entire barrage. Ukrainian President Zelenskyy condemned the assault, describing it as a deliberate demonstration of violence. Officials emphasised the urgent need for additional air defence systems and ammunition packages to better intercept incoming ballistic threats.Earlier, Zelenskyy said US negotiators had proposed holding a trilateral meeting involving Ukraine and Russia at the technical level by the end of October, with Kyiv expressing readiness to participate.

. Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha, Harivansh emphasized that Pakistan has no locus-standi to comment on India’s internal affairs. He said this while Exercising the Right of Reply to certain uncalled remarks made by Pakistan on Kashmir while participating in the 153rd Assembly of the Inter-Parliamentary Union in Arusha, Tanzania, yesterday. He asserted that Kashmir is an integral and inalienable part of India.During the Assembly, Lok Sabha MP Anurag Singh Thakur participated in the meeting of the Standing Committee on Democracy and Human Rights. While Lok Sabha MP Kamaljeet Sehrawat attended the meeting of the Standing Committee on Peace and International Security and participated in the debate on Shaping peaceful futures: Parliamentary diplomacy, mediation and dialogue for lasting peace. Rajya Sabha MP Dr Sasmit Patra participated in a panel discussion of the Standing Committee on Peace and International Security on the “Role of parliaments in securing peace in the age of military artificial intelligence.” He also took part in the deliberations of the Standing Committee on Democracy and Human Rights and contributed to drafting the resolution on the rights and empowerment of persons with disabilities.

. Benchmark domestic equity indices snapped their two-day rising streak today. The Sensex fell 429 points, or 0.6 per cent to close at 72,639. The Nifty dropped 173 points, or nearly 0.8 per cent to settle at 22,603.In the broader market at the National Stock Exchange, the Midcap 100 index lost over 0.6 per cent while the Smallcap 100 index advanced 0.3 per cent.In the Sensex pack, 26 of the 30 constituent companies logged losses. Among the top underperformers, Titan shed three and a half per cent, BEL dropped 2.2 per cent and Asian Paints fell 2.1 per cent. In contrast, Kotak Mahindra Bank surged 2.2 per cent, Bharti Airtel rose over 1.3 per cent and ICICI Bank jumped over 1.1 per cent.In the sectoral indices on the BSE, 24 out of 28 sectors edged downward. Among the top laggards, Metal shed nearly two and a half per cent, Consumer Durables fell over 1.8 per cent, and Realty dropped more than 1.7 per cent. In contrast, PSU Banks gained 1.2 per cent, Housing Finance as well as Telecommunication jumped over 0.9 per cent, and Hospitals added more than 0.2 per cent.The overall market breadth at the BSE was negative, as shares of 2360 companies declined, 2013 advanced and 241 remained unchanged.

. Paralympic champions Pramod Bhagat and Bhavina Patel will lead the Indian contingent as flag bearers at the Opening Ceremony of the Asian Para Games, which will get underway later this month. The Games will be held from 18th to 24th October at Aichi-Nagoya in Japan, with athletes from across Asia competing in the grand sporting event. Para badminton star Pramod Bhagat has won six Asian Para Games medals, including two gold and four bronze, between 2014 and 2023. Para table tennis player Bhavina Patel has also won two Asian Para Games medals – a silver and a bronze – between 2018 and 2023.Calling it a proud moment, Ms Patel said carrying the Tricolour means representing something much bigger than oneself.The Paralympic Committee of India (PCI) will formally see off the Indian contingent at a special ceremony tomorrow. Sports Minister Mansukh Mandaviya will attend the event as Chief Guest, with Minister of State for Youth Affairs and Sports Raksha Nikhil Khadse as Guest of Honour.PCI President Devendra Jhajharia said Bhagat and Patel are exceptional champions whose achievements and resilience make them fitting representatives of the Indian contingent.

. Veteran actor Nana Patekar will be cremated with full state honours at Donje near Pune today at 4 PM. The Maharashtra government has decided to accord him a state funeral. Nana Patekar had a close association with his farmhouse at Donje, where his last rites will be performed.Patekar, known for his powerful screen presence, passed away early this morning at his residence in Goa following a massive cardiac arrest. He was 75. After he was found unconscious following sudden discomfort, he was rushed to Manipal Hospital. Doctors attempted to revive him with CPR for around 45 minutes but could not save him. He was declared dead at around 5:20 AM.The actor, known for his acclaimed performances in Hindi and Marathi cinema, had a career spanning several decades and was a recipient of three National Film Awards.

. The conflict in Yemen has further escalated, with the Houthis claiming missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia and government-held areas of Yemen.Saudi Arabia said three people were killed and 36 injured in attacks on Abha International Airport and King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh on October 6 and 7. Two women, a Moroccan and an Algerian resident, were killed in Abha, while a Sudanese resident was killed in Riyadh.The Houthis said they targeted King Khalid International Airport with a ballistic missile, disrupting airport operations, while Saudi Arabia’s coalition said it intercepted missiles targeting Khamis Mushait and north of Riyadh. The coalition later said it destroyed a ballistic missile launch platform in Sanaa.In Yemen, the Transport Ministry in Aden said the Houthis targeted Aden International Airport with two ballistic missiles and several explosive-laden drones. Meanwhile, the UAE strongly condemned the attacks and reaffirmed its solidarity with Saudi Arabia.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated the 10th edition of the India Mobile Congress (IMC) at Yashobhoomi in New Delhi. The four-day event, which began yesterday, showcases India’s remarkable progress in telecommunications, digital connectivity and technological innovation. The theme of IMC 2026 is “Scale Without Boundaries”, reflecting India’s growing capabilities in digital innovation, next-generation connectivity and technology-led growth.Speaking on the occasion, Prime Minister Modi said that the India Mobile Congress platform has witnessed the evolution of the telecom sector and digital connectivity in India. He said that 5G connectivity has now reached every district of the country. Mr Modi added that there are now more than five lakh 50 thousand base stations operating 5G connectivity across India.On the occasion, Union Communications Minister Jyotiraditya Scindia said that Prime Minister Modi has always emphasised that technology must reach not only the last village but every single citizen. He added that the proliferation of technology can only take place when it is affordable and inclusive. Mr Scindia said that in 2014, one gigabyte of data cost 268 rupees, whereas today it costs only around eight rupees, making India one of the countries with the cheapest data in the world.The Minister lauded equipment manufacturers, telecom operators and every employee of the telecom sector for their contribution to making 5G the fastest-adopted 5G technology in the world. He said that India today has 550 million 5G users and that IMC 2026 will showcase India’s digital capabilities.India Mobile Congress focuses on innovation and next-generation digital infrastructure, technology-led economic growth, inclusive digital access, and the development of secure and resilient digital ecosystems. The event has brought together global technology leaders, policymakers, industry experts, startups, investors and innovators to explore emerging opportunities across the digital ecosystem.The event will also expand its sectoral focus to four new domains: smart mobility, stadium experiences, industrial robotics and transport technology. More than 1.5 lakh attendees from over 100 countries, along with over 500 partners and exhibitors and 600 startups, are participating in the event.

. In Badminton, Indian Men’s Doubles pair Krishna Prasad Garaga and Pruthvi Krishnamurthy Roy advanced to the second round of the Arctic Open Super 500 tournament at Vantaa in Finland, today.The Indian duo produced a stunning upset, defeating fifth seeds He Ji Ting and Ren Xiang Yu of China 10-21, 21-18, 22-20 in a closely fought opening-round match.However, in Men’s Singles, HS Prannoy suffered an early exit, losing 10-21, 9-21 to fourth-seeded Dane Anders Antonsen.In Women’s Singles, two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu advanced to the pre-quarterfinals after defeating Canada’s Wen Yu Zhang 21-8, 21-11.Tanvi Sharma also progressed to the second round, beating Taiwan’s Chiu Pin Chian 21-15, 21-17. However, Isharani Baruah went down 10-21, 15-21 to top seed Ratchanok Intanon of Thailand.Unnati Hooda, Ashmita Chaliha and Malvika Bansod also bowed out in the opening rounds. Unnati lost to China’s Han Qian Xi, while Ashmita was beaten by Denmark’s Line Christophersen in a tight three-game contest. Malvika went down to Scotland’s Kirsty Gilmour in straight games.

. The Government has debunked a post circulating on social media claiming that India’s regulatory framework for satellite communication services is being applied in a discriminatory manner.The Ministry of Communications said that India’s regulatory framework for satellite communication services is fair and non-discriminatory. It added that the Government has put in place a fair and non-discriminatory authorisation framework for all telecommunication services, including satellite communication services.Under this framework, telecom licences have been granted to three Global Mobile Personal Communications by Satellite (GMPCS) service providers based on non-geosynchronous satellite orbit-based satellite communications.Under the terms and conditions of the licence, every such licensee is required to demonstrate compliance with security conditions. The Ministry said this is aimed at ensuring that the services provided meet various security requirements to ensure the safety of all users and their data.

. India T20I captain Shreyas Iyer has climbed to a career-best seventh spot in the latest ICC rankings for the shortest format, while ODI skipper Shubman Gill has retained the top position in the ODI format.Shreyas Iyer climbed 18 places to a career-best seventh in the ICC T20I batting rankings after scoring an unbeaten 102 off 43 balls, making him India’s third-highest-ranked batter in the format. Ishan Kishan and Abhishek Sharma remain in the top two, while Tilak Varma is in 10th position.Axar Patel rose 16 places to seventh among T20I bowlers after taking six wickets in three matches.In ODIs, Shubman Gill retained the top spot after scoring an unbeaten 223 against the West Indies, reaching a career-best 841 rating points. Virat Kohli slipped to third, while KL Rahul jumped seven places to 10th position after scoring a swashbuckling hundred in the third ODI against the West Indies.

. Russian missiles and drones pounded Kyiv and a dozen other Ukrainian regions overnight, killing 19 civilians, including four children, and wounding around 60 others. Ukrainian officials said the worst-hit area was Pryluky in the northern Chernihiv region, where a Russian strike destroyed an apartment building, killing 13 people, including four children, and injuring about 50. Deaths were also reported in Kyiv and other cities. In Kremenchuk, two people were killed and seven injured.President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Russia had carried out a massive and deliberate attack. He said Ukraine urgently needs more air-defence systems, particularly Patriot missiles, to counter Russian ballistic missiles.Russia’s Defence Ministry said its forces had targeted Ukrainian defence-industrial facilities, as well as port and ship-repair facilities in the Odesa region.Ukraine has also continued long-range strikes inside Russia, targeting oil facilities and military sites.The latest attacks come as Russia and Ukraine remain locked in a prolonged aerial war, with diplomatic efforts offering little prospect of an immediate end to the conflict.

. India’s women’s cricket captain Harmanpreet Kaur has stepped down as captain across all three formats. The 37-year-old announced her decision after a BCCI review meeting in Guwahati. Harmanpreet led India to its maiden ODI World Cup title last year and also guided the team to gold at the Asian Games. She captained India in five Tests, 51 ODIs and 155 T20Is, having led the T20 side since 2016 and taken charge of the ODI team in 2022. Harmanpreet will continue to represent India as a player across formats.

. External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Côte d’Ivoire’s Vice Prime Minister and Defence Minister, Téné Birahima Ouattara, in Abidjan last night. In a social media post, Dr. Jaishankar said the two sides discussed their growing defence partnership, underpinned by mutual trust, capacity building and shared interests. They also exchanged views on opportunities to further strengthen cooperation in defence and counter-terrorism, including through training, capacity building and enhanced institutional exchanges.The External Affairs Minister also held comprehensive discussions with Côte d’Ivoire’s Minister of State for Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Nialé Kaba, focusing on advancing bilateral cooperation across trade, investment, infrastructure, agriculture, healthcare and people-to-people ties. In a social media post, the External Affairs Minister underlined that India-Côte d’Ivoire cooperation would remain people-centric and would be guided by the priorities of the West African country. The two sides also discussed ways to deepen engagement in multilateral fora.The meeting in Abidjan is part of Jaishankar’s five-day official visit to Ghana, Côte d’Ivoire and Ethiopia, aimed at strengthening India’s ties with the three African nations. Earlier during his visit to Ghana, Jaishankar held talks with Ghanaian Foreign Minister Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa on expanding the bilateral Comprehensive Partnership.

. In the forex market, the rupee depreciated by 36 paise to close at 96 rupees and 78 paise against the US dollar.The dollar index, which indicates US dollar’s strength against a basket of six other leading currencies, was trading at 102.34 in intra-day trade.

. The Indian Meteorological Department (IMD) hasissued redalert for extremely heavy rainfall over isolated places of Chhattisgarh, Coastal Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Telangana for the next two days. The Met Department has predicted heavy rainfall over Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Meghalaya, Bihar, Jharkhand, Kerala, Maharashtra, West Bengal and Sikkim tomorrow. The weather department also forecast thunderstorms accompanied with highly gusty winds over Madhya Pradesh and Parts of North-East tomorrow.For Delhi, IMD said the national capital will witness mostly clear skies with no rain. The maximum temperature in Delhi is expected to be around 34 to 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum temperature of 23 to 25 degrees Celsius.

. Members of the Asian Games Gold Medal winning Indian Hockey team landed at Amritsar airport to a rousing welcome today morning. They were greeted by enthusiastic citizens, sports fans, Punjab Hockey Association officials besides their parents with the drum beats, garlands and bouquets.Captain Harmanpreet, who scored two goals, expressed immense pride and joy at winning the Gold. He stated that winning and then retaining any title is the result of the collective effort and dedication of the entire team. He also underlined that securing a direct Olympic berth will prove to be very beneficial for the team, as they will now have ample time to assess their shortcomings and prepare for the Olympics. He also congratulated the Indian Women Hockey team as well for winning Gold in the Asian Games. Others who landed include Jugraj Singh, Hardik and Manpreet Singh.The Indian team won the historic Gold by defeating Malaysia by a comprehensive 5-1 margin and sealed the berth for Los Angeles Olympics- 2028 also.

. Today is World Cotton Day. This day is celebrated annually on October 7 to highlight the global economic, social, and environmental importance of cotton. The theme for this year is Cotton for Good: Building Prosperity Through Trade, Transformation and Partnership. Sharing a video message, Union Textiles Minister Giriraj Singh extended greetings to everyone associated with this sector.He said that this day honours farmers who cultivate cotton in the fields, thereby enabling employment for workers across the entire value chain, whether in spinning mills, ginneries, textile manufacturing units, or garment factories. He informed that 60 lakh farmers in the country are engaged in cotton cultivation. He underlined that countless small enterprises are linked to the handloom industries that not only operate domestically but also export their products.

. President Droupadi Murmu, Vice President C. P. Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi expressed grief over the demise of veteran Hindi and Marathi film actor Nana Patekar, who passed away at the age of 75 after suffering a severe cardiac arrest at his residence in Goa this morning.President Murmu praised Mr Patekar’s powerful and evocative performances, saying he brought a wide range of human experiences to life and left a lasting impression on audiences. She also appreciated his commitment to social service and said his passing is a great loss to Indian cinema.Vice President Radhakrishnan described Mr Patekar as a versatile and immensely talented artist whose depth, sensitivity and authenticity enriched Indian cinema. He said the actor’s contribution will be remembered by generations of cinema lovers.Prime Minister Modi said Mr Patekar brought remarkable versatility and creativity to every role and left an immense contribution to Hindi and Marathi cinema. He said the actor’s passing has left a deep void and conveyed his condolences to the bereaved family, friends and admirers.

. The 57th GST Council meeting is underway at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman is chairing the meeting. Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis, Karnataka Chief Minister D. K. Shivakumar, Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, Haryana Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini, and Finance Ministers of States and Union Territories are also attending the meeting.The GST Council meeting will discuss policy reforms to resolve GST disputes and improve the flow of input tax credit, with the aim of reducing the time and cost of compliance. Sources in the Finance Ministry said that the government will propose a five-pronged plan for the next set of reforms to the Goods and Services Tax (GST) system. These reforms are aimed at automating and easing many of the current administrative bottlenecks in the GST system and reducing the compliance burden, especially for small businesses.The five-pronged proposal covers process reforms, structural reforms, ease of living and doing business, exports of services, and e-commerce. Some of the key changes proposed involve automatic invoice matching between buyers and sellers, reducing paperwork around claiming input tax credits (ITC), reducing the number of times small taxpayers have to file returns, and removing multi-state registrations for small businesses.The last, 56th meeting of the GST Council was held in September last year. During the meeting, the Council approved rate rationalisation with a focus on the common man, labour-intensive industries, farmers and agriculture, health, and key drivers of the economy.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over coastal and South Interior Karnataka, Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry for the next 2-3 days. The IMD said thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds may prevail over Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttarakhand, Sub-Himalayan West Bengal, Sikkim, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura tomorrow. Meanwhile, Konkan and Goa may experience Hot and Humid weather tomorrow.

. Tripura State Government has allotted 30.30 acres of land to the Tripura Cricket Association (TCA) for setting up a cricket academy in the state. The TCA has been asked to deposit 6 crore 81 lakh 75 thousand rupees with the Revenue Department towards the cost of the land.TCA Secretary Subrata Dey announced the development at a press conference held today at the Club House of MBB Stadium. He said, the proposed Cricket academy will be established on 30.30 acres of land in the Sekerkote area.The academy is expected to significantly benefit cricketers from across Tripura by providing them with better training and development facilities. Subrata Dey expressed hope that the land transfer process would be completed very soon.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) today said the recent 25-basis-point repo rate hike could moderate bank credit growth, which is currently above 18 per cent, but is unlikely to have a significant impact on overall economic expansion.RBI Governor Sanjay Malhotra said credit growth is expected to remain strong and continue supporting economic activity, adding that minor fluctuations in its pace would not materially affect the economy.The RBI has shifted its policy stance to calibrated tightening and indicated that rate cuts are unlikely in the near term. Malhotra said monetary policy decisions would primarily be guided by domestic growth and inflation conditions, while global developments would also be taken into account.The Governor said the renewed escalation of the West Asia conflict, volatile crude oil prices, rising bond yields in advanced economies and an appreciating US dollar have weakened global economic sentiment and increased financial market volatility. He said global growth is expected to slow in 2026 despite remaining resilient, while higher energy and food prices are likely to push up inflation and prompt further monetary policy tightening by major central banks.

India has joined the United States and 13 other economies in signing a joint ministerial statement calling for measures to address structural excess capacity and production and curb non-market policies that distort global markets. The joint ministerial statement, signed by the 15 participating economies, was released by the Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR) last night, following discussions among G20 Trade Ministers in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, on September 30 and October 1, 2026.In a statement, the countries called for measures to eliminate structural excess capacity and production, including by ending non-market policies that distort markets. They noted that more countries are acting to protect their industries, workers and economies from such distortions. They stressed that cooperation, information-sharing and coordinated action would make these efforts more effective.The signatories include Argentina, Australia, Canada, the European Union, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, the Republic of Korea, Mexico, Poland, Türkiye, the United Kingdom and the United States.

. The second India- European Free Trade Association (EFTA) Prosperity Summit was held in New Delhi today. The summit brought together senior Indian and EFTA officials, business leaders and industry representatives to discuss trade, investment and economic cooperation. President of Switzerland Guy Parmelin who is currently on a three day visit to India was present in the Summit. He arrived in New Delhi on Monday. India and the  EFTA, comprising Switzerland, Iceland, Liechtenstein and Norway, mark one year since the implementation of their Trade and Economic Partnership Agreement.Talking to reporters after attending the Summit, Information and Broadcasting Minister  Ashwini Vaishnaw said that  productive discussions took place  between the Ministers and businesses on both sides.Mr Vaishnaw said that the European countries today considers  India as a major hub for innovation and manufacturing. He said, several kinds of partnerships are being established with India, which will also facilitate the exchange of technology. He said, this is expected to create approximately one million new jobs in total and generate new opportunities for the youth.

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Bhupender Yadav held a meeting with Australia’s Minister for Climate Change and Energy and COP31 President of Negotiations, Chris Bowen, in Fiji.The meeting was held on the sidelines of Pre-COP31. During the meeting, both sides discussed priority agenda items for the upcoming COP31.In a social media post, Mr Yadav said that he reiterated India’s commitment to a constructive approach and to working with the COP31 President of Negotiations towards a balanced and ambitious outcome.

. Athletes from the Army Sports Institute (ASI), Pune, won 12 medals at the Asian Games, accounting for 60 per cent of the 20 medals won by Indian Army athletes. A total of 25 ASI athletes were part of the Indian contingent.In Athletics, Gulveer Singh won three medals, including silver in the 1,500 and 10,000 metres and bronze in the 5,000 metres. Sawan Barwal won silver in the marathon, while Sarvesh Kushare secured silver in the high jump. Dharmveer was part of the bronze-winning 4×400 metre relay team.In Boxing, Sub Ankush won gold, while Sub Narender and Hav Kapil won bronze. In Archery, Sub Dhiraj secured two silver medals and set an Asian record with a score of 698 out of 720. Sub Deepak Punia won bronze in the 97-kilogram freestyle wrestling event. The performance highlights the Army Sports Institute’s sustained efforts in athlete development, specialist coaching, sports science and infrastructure under the Army’s Mission Olympics programme.

The Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas conducted a special inspection drive in Delhi to assess road dust and effectiveness of road cleaning operations across the city.The Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change has informed that the commission deployed four flying squad teams for the inspection which was carried out yesterday. The Flying Squad Teams inspected 25 road stretches covering approximately 35 kilometres of the Inner and Outer ring road which come under the jurisdiction of the Public Works Department (PWD), Delhi.The Ministry highlighted that the inspections, which were meant to seek strict implementation of road cleaning and dust mitigation measures, found 17 cases of violation. These violations include accumulation of construction and demolition waste and high visible road dust across inspected road stretches.CAQM has directed PWD, Delhi and other concerned agencies to take appropriate corrective measures to control road dust on priority basis. It also added the inspection shall continue under Operation Clean Air across Delhi-NCR to assess on-ground implementation of various air pollution abatement measures.

. The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast heavy rainfall over Andaman and Nicobar Islands, South Interior Karnataka and Uttarakhand tomorrow. It has also predicted thunderstorms accompanied with lightning and gusty winds over North Eastern parts of India, including Assam, Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura, during the next two days. According to IMD, Himachal Pradesh, Rajasthan, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry, Karaikal, Andhra Pradesh, Bihar, Madhya Maharashtra, Marathwada, Odisha and Telangana are also likely to witness similar weather conditions tomorrow.

. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is completing 25 years in public service, a journey defined by the mantra of Jan Seva Se Desh Seva, and a relentless commitment that continues. Guided by this vision for Seva and Sushasan, the Government has been ceaselessly working towards achieving the goal of a Viksit Bharat by 2047. Through inclusive development and social empowerment, this dedication is transforming lives. Today, in our special series, we bring you an instance of how this vision has been translated into creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff.Earlier, India’s three armed services – Army, Navy and the Air Force – planned, trained, procured and advised the government separately. Proposals for greater jointness had been made repeatedly since the Kargil Review Committee of 1999 and the Group of Ministers that followed it, but no single officer held authority across all three services. On the 15th of August 2019, Prime Minister Narendra Modi, in his Independence Day address, announced the creation of the post of Chief of Defence Staff from the ramparts of the Red Fort. Prime Minister Modi said this will lead to better coordination among the three services.The Cabinet approved the decision in December 2019, along with a new Department of Military Affairs within the Ministry of Defence for the CDS to head.  Talking to Akashvani News, retired Lt General Sanjay Kulkarni said the appointment of CDS made it possible for the government to have one point of contact for advice on allmiltarymatters.After the formation of the post of CDS, all three forces have now got effective leadership at the top level.

. Science and Technology Minister Dr Jitendra Singh has said that critical minerals are key to India’s energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. The Minister said this while addressing a special plenary of the 3rd Global Summit on Advanced Materials, Critical Minerals, and Metals in New Delhi. Dr Singh said that critical minerals and metals will be a driving component of the next phase of technological development, with their importance extending beyond mining to energy security, industrial competitiveness and national security. He said that the global economy is undergoing a paradigm shift, with clean energy, electric mobility, semiconductors, telecommunications, aerospace, defence and nuclear energy emerging as major drivers of technological and industrial transformation. He added, India is now participating in this global discourse with much greater confidence and is preparing to assume a larger global role.Dr. Singh has called for early industry linkage with research and innovation, saying potential industry partners should be brought on board right from the beginning. He further said that a healthy synergy among research, industry, government and the non-government sector is essential for sustaining startups and entrepreneurs. The Minister also highlighted on building domestic capabilities for energy security as the world moves towards cleaner and greener sources of energy. He said that India’s next phase of growth in strategic technologies and materials will depend on working together of all stakeholders.

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) today announced a series of developmental and regulatory measures aimed at enhancing customers’ convenience and strengthening engagement with participants in financial markets. Under the Account Aggregator framework, the RBI has decided to introduce interoperability among NBFC-Account Aggregators (NBFC-AAs). The move will allow customers to access and share their financial information across different Financial Information Providers through any NBFC-AA of their choice.The RBI has also facilitated SEBI-regulated depositories to include bank deposit account information in their Consolidated Account Statements (CAS) through NBFC-AAs. This will enable demat account holders to view information on their demat holdings and bank deposits at a single place.Customers without demat accounts will also continue to be able to obtain a consolidated view of their financial information and share it through NBFC-AAs.Both measures are expected to be implemented by December 31, 2026.Separately, the RBI has decided to constitute a Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets amid the rapid evolution of financial markets and related infrastructure.The committee will provide a structured platform for engagement between the RBI and market participants and stakeholders on policy and operational matters relating to money, government securities and foreign exchange markets, along with their respective derivative markets and infrastructure.

Air Chief Marshal AP Singh highlighted the Indian Air Force’s growing capabilities and stressed that its true strength lies in its air warriors rather than merely in advanced equipment and technology.Addressing the Indian Air Force (IAF) Day celebrations at Hindon Air Base in Ghaziabad, Air Chief Marshal Singh emphasised the role of air power in protecting national interests and described the Indian Air Force as the custodian of the skies. He also said that the IAF understands its role and responsibilities and is always alert, committed and ready to meet any contingency.The Air Chief Marshal also recalled the IAF’s combat operations during Operation Sindoor. He said that the country saw firsthand the destructive power as well as the effective air defence operations of the Air Force during the operation. He added that ‘Infallible, Impervious and Precise’ was not merely a tagline but represented the strength and resolve of the force. Mr Singh also highlighted the strengthening culture of ownership and accountability across the force and expressed satisfaction over the upholding of the core values of the defence services.The Indian Air Force also displayed its prowess as it held a massive parade at Hindon Air Base to celebrate the 94th Indian Air Force Day. Meanwhile, the IAF Chief inspected the parade at Hindon Air Base. The theme of this year’s celebration is ‘Indian Air Force – Infallible, Impervious and Precise’. Group Captain Manish Sharma commanded the parade. Chief of the Army Staff, General Dhiraj Seth, and Chief of the Naval Staff, Admiral K. Swaminathan, were also present on the occasion.The celebrations come as the Indian Air Force undergoes a major transformation to meet emerging security challenges.As part of this year’s celebrations, the main aerial show will be held in Varanasi, where IAF pilots will showcase the nation’s formidable air power through breathtaking aerial manoeuvres over the holy city.

. India’s live events sector grew by 44 per cent over the last one year, with around 34 thousand events held across the country. Secretary of the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting Chanchal Kumar said this, addressing the 5th meeting of the Live Events Development Cell in New Delhi today. He said that the sector is now supporting more than one crore livelihoods. The Secretary also said the Government has set an ambitious target of doubling the sector by 2030, with the potential to generate 15-20 million direct and ancillary jobs.The meeting reviewed the implementation of the Single Window Clearances Portal for the live event industry on the India Cine Hub (ICH) portal. States and UTs were asked to designate Nodal Officers, nominate authorised officers from departments, integrate departmental and local licensing systems with the ICH Portal, route the complete licence lifecycle through the portal, onboard live event venues and notify live event licensing as a time-bound public service.

The country’s automobile retail sales rose 31.8 per cent year on year to over 25 lakh units in September this year, marking the best-ever first half of fiscal year, according to a report released by the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations (FADA).Passenger vehicle (PV) sales grew 32.1 per cent year on year in September, while commercial vehicle (CV) sales increased 37.6 per cent. Two-wheeler sales jumped 33 per cent, while three-wheeler sales rose 22 per cent over the same period.

. India and Uruguay will face each other today in a FIFA international friendly football match at the Yuva Bharati Krirangan in Salt Lake. India had earlier played out a 1-1 draw against Panama and suffered a 0-4 defeat to Brazil on Saturday. Learning from the mistakes of their previous match, the Indian team will be looking to put up a strong performance against two-time world champions Uruguay in their final friendly. India coach Khalid Jamil said there was a lack of coordination among the players in the last match. He said the players will remain alert from the very first minute against Uruguay.Uruguay coach Diego Forlán, meanwhile, said India have several skilled players capable of putting their opponents under pressure. He added that Uruguay are not taking the Indian team lightly.
